approachLogic:
The assignment funnels benchmarks into one recommended model and a Terms of Reference to build it. EY has already cut the first stage. Our scan of 31 brands, networks and mechanisms, sorted into seven archetypes and rated against CI's own design aims, was completed before this proposal was written. Activity One therefore begins as verification and deep-dive, not discovery.

That changes the arithmetic of twelve weeks. A conventional bid spends weeks one to five finding out who is out there. We spend them verifying published figures against primary sources, running thirteen deep-dives and interviewing the secretariats that publish nothing. Interview requests go out in week one rather than week four. This matters because Boundless Southern Africa, Africa's Eden Tourism, The Long Run and Preferred Hotel Group publish neither fees nor outcomes, and a cold approach to a regional secretariat takes three to four weeks to land.

The head start also fixes the structure. CI's nine model-elaboration headings become the template every deep-dive is written to, so benchmark evidence drops straight into option design. CI's design aims become the nine-column scoring matrix, already built and populated for 31 cases. Design and evaluation are the same frame applied twice, first to benchmarks and then to options.

The budget sets depth, not ambition. Eight case studies, two of them clustered, and five light-touch checks is what US$40,000 over twelve desk-based weeks will carry. We said so in writing before being asked.
evidenceEngine:
The scan profiles 31 benchmarks across seven archetypes: shared service, site standard, enterprise mark, place marketer, curator and distributor, portfolio umbrella and revenue engine. Each is set out on scale and offer, funding, governance and read-across, then rated against nine criteria drawn from CI's design aims. Thirteen earn deep-dives, eight as case studies and five as light-touch checks.

Compressing Activity One buys three things. Interviews start in week one, so the commercial terms nobody publishes have eleven weeks to surface rather than six. The week five situational analysis carries verified evidence and seven tested POV signals instead of a literature review. And the option set arrives at CI in week six, built from archetypes that already exist on paper, so CI screens real configurations in a two-hour session rather than waiting for them to be invented.
stakeholderEngagement: No travel, so every interview and session runs virtually. We target sixteen interviews with twelve as the floor. Priority sits with the organisations that publish nothing: the Boundless Southern Africa secretariat on eighteen years of cost and trade adoption, Africa's Eden Tourism in Botswana on tiers and fees, the KAZA Secretariat on Rivers of Life hub adoption and UniVisa uptake, NRT, NACSO and MMWCA on cost per conservancy, and The Long Run on fee levels and time to GER. On the build, host or borrow question we approach Preferred Hotel Group for Beyond Green and SLH for the Considerate Collection. Slovenia Green, Tourism Australia on Signature Experiences, SANParks on Wild Card revenue splits and EUROPARC on why the Charter fell from 164 areas to 91 complete the list. Two virtual presentations follow the week ten draft, with a written appetite instrument for those who cannot attend.

weeks.work: Kick-off with CI's Tourism Technical Assistance team. Confirm the fifteen priority areas, the stakeholder map, parallel Keystone brand work and the scope boundary that excludes creating brands and identities. Agree the evaluation frame and the week six screening gate. Issue interview requests to nine named secretariats and platforms.
weeks.output: Kick-off note; data and interview request register; draft evaluation frame; risk and assumption log opened.
weeks.ciInvolvement: Ninety-minute virtual kick-off. Supply the list of fifteen priority areas with managing authorities. Broker introductions to the named secretariats.

weeks.work: Finalise the inception report: workplan, refined method, evaluation frame, interview programme with named targets, and the risk and assumption log. Begin Tier 1 desk verification on Boundless Southern Africa, Africa's Eden Tourism and KAZA.
weeks.output: Deliverable 1: Inception Report, carrying the 31-benchmark long-list, the archetype map and the rating matrix as Annex A.
weeks.ciInvolvement: Review and approve the inception report within five working days. Confirm outstanding interview introductions.

weeks.work: Deep-dive block A, the African set: Boundless Southern Africa, Africa's Eden Tourism, KAZA Rivers of Life and UniVisa, and the conservancy association cluster of NRT, NACSO and MMWCA. Verify published figures against primary sources. First five to six interviews.
weeks.output: Four Tier 1 case studies in draft, each written to CI's nine model-elaboration headings; source grading register populated.
weeks.ciInvolvement: Chase outstanding introductions. Confirm access to CI's own MMWCA and Maasai Mara Rescue Fund material.

weeks.work: Deep-dive block B, the global set: The Long Run, Slovenia Green, Signature Experiences of Australia and the commercial collectives cluster on the build, host or borrow question. Five light-touch checks on SANParks Wild Card, site standards, enterprise marks, Alpine Pearls and Visit Rwanda. Build the crowding and gap map.
weeks.output: Four further case studies, five light-touch checks, the crowding and gap map; cumulative interviews at ten to twelve.
weeks.ciInvolvement: Nominate two or three priority areas whose park authorities should be interviewed in weeks eight and nine.

weeks.work: Synthesis and drafting: the archetype spectrum, the verified rating matrix against CI's design aims, good practice, failure patterns, the gaps a model must fill and the design implications carried into Activity Two. Partner-led quality gate before issue.
weeks.output: Deliverable 2: Draft Situational Analysis and Best Practice Assessment, with a one-page set of principles for sustainable protected-area branding.
weeks.ciInvolvement: Receive the draft. Consolidated written comments due by end of week six.

weeks.work: Set the three cross-cutting switches against archetype anchors and build four candidate configurations. Screen them with CI to carry three plus one reserve. Start the cost-to-serve model, harvesting unit economics from the case studies.
weeks.output: Option architecture note; screening decision log recording what was dropped and why; financial model skeleton.
weeks.ciInvolvement: Two-hour virtual option screening session. Consolidated written comments on Deliverable 2.

weeks.work: Elaborate headings one to five for each carried option: services and offer, expected results, stakeholders, information and cash flows, and funding needs over time. Build the ten-year cost-to-serve and revenue-stack model.
weeks.output: Draft option canvases; financial model version one with funding-gap curves and a years-to-self-funding figure per option.
weeks.ciInvolvement: One-hour checkpoint on the draft canvases. Flag any revenue engine CI judges politically or reputationally unviable.

weeks.work: Elaborate headings six to nine: governance and management structures, potential funders and investors, case studies and lessons, and pros and cons across CI's six stakeholder lenses. Appetite interviews with payer-side stakeholders including lodges, operators, a national tourism board and the hosting platforms.
weeks.output: Complete nine-heading elaboration per option; governance and legal vehicle options; funder and investor map.
weeks.ciInvolvement: Introductions to two or three park authorities and one co-management partner. Confirm the invite list for the week ten session.

weeks.work: Score the options on the nine-criterion matrix at weights agreed with CI before scoring. Sensitivity test the assumptions that flip the result. Select and justify the preferred model with a staged pathway. Draft the report and build the presentation pack. Partner-led quality gate.
weeks.output: Draft report and presentation pack ready for issue; scoring workbook with sensitivity runs and a documented weighting decision.
weeks.ciInvolvement: Thirty-minute session to agree the criteria weights. Confirm attendees and logistics for both stakeholder sessions.

weeks.work: Issue Deliverable 3 on day one of the week. Run stakeholder session one with CI and core Keystone partners, ninety minutes, against a structured appetite instrument asking what would have to be true to join, fund or pay. Open the Activity Three skeleton.
weeks.output: Deliverable 3: draft report and presentation on brand delivery models; session one record and appetite evidence.
weeks.ciInvolvement: Circulate the pre-read on receipt. Convene and chair session one late in the week.

weeks.work: Stakeholder session two early in the week with park authorities, a national tourism board, a co-management partner and private sector trade. Log every comment with a disposition. Draft Activity Three: next steps, further research, the sensitisation plan and the Terms of Reference for designing the selected model.
weeks.output: Adaptation and disposition log; draft Activity Three pack including the draft Terms of Reference.
weeks.ciInvolvement: Convene session two early in the week. Consolidated written comments due by Wednesday, leaving seven working days to final.

weeks.work: Combine Activity One, Two and Three into one report. Work the disposition log through the text, showing what changed and why. Finalise the financial model and the Terms of Reference. Final quality assurance and partner sign-off.
weeks.output: Deliverable 4: Final Report, final presentation pack, financial model and the Terms of Reference annex.

methodSteps.step: Inception alignment and the long-lead evidence request
methodSteps.what: A ninety-minute kick-off confirms CI's fifteen priority areas, the stakeholder map and any parallel Keystone brand work. We agree the evaluation frame, the screening gate and the scope boundary that keeps brand creation out. Interview requests then go to nine named secretariats and platforms in week one, with CI brokering introductions. The inception report carries the 31-benchmark long-list as Annex A.
methodSteps.why: Interview access is the binding constraint on evidence quality, and a cold approach to a regional secretariat takes three to four weeks. Issuing requests in week one rather than week four is the difference between citing a published activity report and citing what the secretariat actually spends.

methodSteps.step: Source verification and grading of the long-list
methodSteps.what: Every figure in the scan is re-checked against its primary source and graded on three levels: verified with the organisation, published primary, or secondary report. Each number in the report then carries its grade and its date. Nothing below the top two grades is allowed to drive the base case of the financial model.
methodSteps.why: The scan states plainly that its figures are as published and unverified with the organisations concerned. Grading turns that honesty into a control. It also stops stale numbers, such as NRT's 2016 fundraising or the 2017 ECST network count, from carrying weight they cannot bear.

methodSteps.step: Thirteen deep-dives written to CI's nine headings
methodSteps.what: Eight case studies, two of them clustered, and five light-touch checks. The African set covers Boundless Southern Africa, Africa's Eden Tourism, KAZA and the conservancy associations. The global set covers The Long Run, Slovenia Green, Signature Experiences of Australia and the commercial collectives. Each is written to the nine headings CI uses for model design.
methodSteps.why: Benchmark evidence then drops straight into option design rather than being re-cut for it. When Activity Two asks what a governance structure or a cash flow looks like, the answer is already drafted in the same shape, with a named precedent and a source grade behind it.

methodSteps.step: The crowding map and the good-practice principles
methodSteps.what: We map what already serves CI's fifteen areas: conservancy associations, national certification schemes, commercial collections and transfrontier brands. Gaps are named, as are the failure patterns, from the ECST's fall from 164 areas to 91 and Alpine Pearls' from 24 villages to 18, to LHW dropping its paid Leaders Club in 2021. The output is a one-page set of branding principles.
methodSteps.why: CI's seventh design aim asks the model to fill gaps rather than duplicate effort. That aim cannot be scored like the others, so it is tested by a map. The failure patterns matter more than the successes; they show what breaks a donor-seeded network once the seed money stops.

methodSteps.what: Each option sets three switches the benchmarks expose: who belongs and who pays; how it crosses borders, whether through one secretariat, national operators, mutual recognition or a cross-border legal vehicle; and how it sits with the national destination brand. Four configurations are built against archetype anchors, then screened with CI to carry three plus a reserve.
methodSteps.why: It forces options that differ in substance rather than in degree, which is what a genuine comparison requires. It also puts the choice in front of CI at week six, when changing direction still costs nothing, and the screening log gives the final report a defensible account of what was dropped.

methodSteps.step: Nine-heading elaboration and the cost-to-serve model
methodSteps.what: Each carried option is elaborated under all nine CI headings. A ten-year financial model sits behind it: cost to serve built bottom-up from benchmark unit economics, and a revenue stack layered from the revenue-engine archetype, running from wild cards and tiered membership to a corporate imagery licence and match funding on the Brand USA pattern.
methodSteps.why: CI asks for specific detail on the financial sustainability model for every option. A funding-gap curve and a years-to-self-funding figure answer that in a form a funder can test. Building the cost side from benchmark unit economics keeps the numbers anchored in observed practice rather than assumed.

methodSteps.what: Options are scored on the same nine-column matrix used for the benchmarks: self-funding, aggregation, conservation-led delivery, data, segments and appeal, national brand fit, cross-border reach, low-capacity fit and African evidence. Weights are agreed with CI before any score is entered. We then publish the two or three assumptions that would flip the result.
methodSteps.why: Agreeing weights before the scores exist removes any suspicion the frame was fitted to a preferred answer. The sensitivity test tells CI what would have to be true for a different model to win, which is the more useful output while commercial terms remain partly unverified.

methodSteps.step: Appetite test, adaptation and the Terms of Reference
methodSteps.what: Two virtual sessions test appetite against a structured instrument asking what would have to be true for each stakeholder to join, fund or pay. Every comment enters an adaptation log with a disposition. The final report then carries Activity Three: next steps, further research, a stakeholder sensitisation plan and a Terms of Reference for designing the selected model.
methodSteps.why: Activity Two requires findings to be presented and the model adapted, which needs a record of who said what and what changed in response. The disposition log supplies it. It also routes late comments into the next-steps register rather than reopening the report, which protects the week twelve date.

qualityAndRisk.risk: Secretariats and commercial platforms do not respond in time. None of LHW, Relais et Chateaux, SLH, Preferred Hotel Group, National Geographic or The Long Run publishes member fees, and no published recognition or booking measures exist for Boundless Southern Africa or KAZA. The economics of the commercial option rest on evidence only they hold.
qualityAndRisk.mitigation: Requests issued in week one, not week four, with CI-brokered introductions named in the inception report. Substitutes pre-identified: the Kenya Wildlife Conservancies Association for MMWCA, Ecotourism Kenya and Botswana's ecotourism certification for Fair Trade Tourism, Preferred Hotel Group where SLH declines. Any figure not obtained is shown as a stated range with its source class, never as fact.

qualityAndRisk.risk: CI's list of fifteen priority areas arrives late or changes, moving the countries, tourism boards and co-management partners the options must serve.
qualityAndRisk.mitigation: The option architecture is built geography-agnostic; geography enters only in the rollout sequencing annex. The list is requested at the week one kick-off with a week three drop-dead, and the assumption set used in its absence is documented in the inception report and revisited at the week six screening gate.

qualityAndRisk.risk: Scope creep towards creating brands and identities, which the terms of reference explicitly exclude at this stage.
qualityAndRisk.mitigation: A written scope boundary in the inception report, restated at every gate. Any request for identity work is logged into the Activity Three Terms of Reference as scoped future work rather than absorbed. Budget is tracked weekly against the four deliverables, with a partner gate before any reallocation.

qualityAndRisk.risk: Thin or unrepresentative attendance at the stakeholder sessions, leaving the appetite finding unevidenced and the preferred model untested against the people who would have to pay for it.
qualityAndRisk.mitigation: Two sessions rather than one, with the invite list agreed at inception and confirmed in week eight. A minimum-coverage rule requires at least one national government or tourism board, one park authority, one co-management partner and one private sector voice. Non-attendees complete a written appetite instrument, recorded in the same log.

qualityAndRisk.risk: The comment window between the week ten draft and the week twelve final compresses, forcing either a late submission or a final report that has not absorbed CI's comments.
qualityAndRisk.mitigation: Deliverable 3 lands on day one of week ten, not at the end. Session two runs early in week eleven and consolidated written comments are due that Wednesday, leaving seven working days. Comments arrive on one template with a disposition column; anything later is logged into the Activity Three next-steps register.

qualityAndRisk.risk: Over-research. Thirty-one benchmarks invite a depth of investigation the budget cannot fund, and the scan itself names thirteen deep-dives plus two further candidates for a later pass.
qualityAndRisk.mitigation: The scoping anchor is fixed and stated to CI: eight case studies, two of them clustered, and five light-touch checks is the most US$40,000 over twelve desk-based weeks can carry. Additional benchmarks enter only as a named, sourced paragraph. Effort is tracked weekly against deliverables.

qualityAndRisk.risk: The option set collapses towards one obvious answer, weakening the comparison CI asked for and leaving the recommendation looking pre-cooked.
qualityAndRisk.mitigation: The three switches force configurations that differ in who pays, how they cross borders and how they sit with national brands. Options are constructed in week six before weights are agreed in week nine. A most-commercial and a most-institutional option are always retained, and the sensitivity test publishes what would have to change for either to win.
